rulings.restated: Input — Is this group publicly traded securities? A security counts only if it is (a) listed on a recognized stock exchange whose quotations are published daily, (b) regularly traded on a national or regional over-the-counter market, or (c) mutual fund shares quoted daily in a national newspaper of general circulation. Answer No for privately held stock, LLC or partnership interests, and for stock that has a ticker symbol but is not regularly traded.
rulings.model: The IRS says 'A security is generally considered to be publicly traded if' and includes 'Certain other securities even though the securities do not meet any of the criteria'; the restatement says a security 'counts only if' it meets (a)-(c) and adds a No for a ticker symbol not regularly traded, which the text does not impose.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; accepted over-refusal. i8283 p. 9, Securities: "A security is generally considered to be publicly traded if the security is (a) listed on a recognized stock exchange whose quotations are published daily; (b) regularly traded on a national or regional over-the-counter market; or (c) quoted daily in a national newspaper of general circulation in the case of mutual fund shares"; i8283 p. 3, Section A, item 2.d: "Certain other securities even though the securities do not meet any of the criteria described in paragraphs 2.a through 2.c above (for more information, see Regulations section 1.170A-13(c)(7)(xi)(B))". The model is right that the PENDING-4 wording ("counts only if", and No for "stock that has a ticker symbol but is not regularly traded") is narrower than the text: it leaves out the 2.d securities, and a security listed on a recognized exchange with daily quotations meets (a) whether or not it trades often. But a No here only sends the group to Section B: gift.section_b (No and a deduction over $5,000) refuses gift.allowed ("A group of similar items over $5,000 requires Section B and a qualified appraisal; publicly traded securities are excepted"), and a group of $5,000 or less is in Section A either way. A Yes the text would deny is not made more likely by the narrowing. So the narrower wording can only refuse a return the tool could support; it never computes a wrong amount, as with gift.section_b. Low: the "ticker symbol but is not regularly traded" sentence could be limited to stock not listed on a recognized exchange (findings file, Low).

rulings.restated:
Input — Does this group need an appraisal or other special treatment: any of the following?

- a deduction over $5,000 (before any income limit), or property worth more than $5,000, for one item or for similar items given to all donees together, other than publicly traded securities
  - similar items: items of the same general category or type, such as coin collections, paintings, books, clothing, jewelry, nonpublicly traded stock, land or buildings
  - publicly traded securities: listed on a recognized stock exchange whose quotations are published daily, regularly traded on a national or regional over-the-counter market, or mutual fund shares quoted daily in a national newspaper
- a noncash contribution reaching you through a Schedule K-1
- vehicles
- pass-through entity interests
- intellectual property
- inventory
- conservation or partial interests
- property with restrictions on its use
- a clothing or household item over $500 not in good used condition
